Whether the corrected response transfers to larger loading and to related ether-containing structures remains unresolved; m110, m123 and m87 should not be assigned a common ether curve.

feedback_interpretation: The latest outcomes reject several proposed reversals while supporting selected structure-specific features. m116 at 52.55 mg grew from 12.54/19.03 at 10/1 through 19.33/29.83 at 20/1 to 36.92/55.54 mL at 50/1. Its historical 50/1 underprediction was about 29.88/39.79 mL, but the current model now predicts a steep extension. I therefore test loading and structural transfer of that correction. m110's 5/1 completion of 12.60 mL was below its measured 10/1 completion of 15.48, weakening the proposed plateau. m54's early completions increased from 6.83 to 8.83 to 9.68 mL, and m175 increased from 8.10 to 10.93, rejecting their forecast minima. The selected m54 extensions examine newly remaining later curvature. Conversely, m91's 70.6 mg completion sequence of 11.80, 9.04 and 11.39 reproduced the minimum seen at 141.2 mg; this argues against imposing monotonic endpoints globally. m186 supports a later onset plateau near 5 mL, while m190's 10/1 completion rose to 24.14 despite nearly unchanged onset from 5/1. m197 retained a long higher-loading baseline: pure-EA and 2/1 completions were 26.43 and 26.95, rejecting the predicted decline. m117's 10/1 record had V1 greater than V2 by approximately 0.075 mL and an unexpectedly late onset; I retain the recorded outcome without treating one anomalous interval as a mechanistic finding. m200 showed a much larger loading association for onset than completion, especially at 2/1, and m36 completion remained near 39–41 mL across measured amounts. These results support endpoint-specific loading tests without establishing a common causal mechanism. m140's proposed onset minimum and m133's weak-eluent completion collapse both failed; their new measured curves were comparatively stable. Finally, the m81 low-loading repeat finished at 11.70 versus the previous 13.00 mL, still above the two approximately 7.95 mL high-loading results. The localized completion association remains plausible, with within-tuple variability limiting interpretation. Another m81 repeat is deferred this round. All historical errors are acquisition-time errors, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale: The batch combines failure repair with measurements of uncovered relationships. Ether extensions test whether a major recent correction transfers across loading and carbonyl environments. The m80, m62 and bromoester experiments target joint endpoint calibration using matched pairs and structural baselines; the confirmed m91 minimum prevents treating endpoint ordering or solvent monotonicity as sufficient scientific explanations. m54 and m130 test specific remaining turning points between measured anchors. The m15, m47, m97 and halogenated-aldehyde panels explore missing response segments where related compounds and current forecasts leave competing possibilities. m197 separates a persistent long baseline from later slope, m117 fills a controlled early gap, and m211 tests transfer of a long heteroaromatic completion tail. Every selected condition tuple is distinct within this batch. Multiple rows per molecule provide interpretable local comparisons, while the connected structural contrasts can inform other remaining Row conditions. Cross-molecule comparisons retain their different recorded amounts and loading-solvent volumes and will not be interpreted as isolated causal tests. This design may improve retrained V1/V2 accuracy through better baselines, ratio curvature, loading sensitivity and structural transfer. Quantile spans are uncalibrated outputs from one predictor, CW distance describes feature-space coverage, and V2 minus V1 is an elution interval width; none serves as a mandatory acquisition rule or an epistemic-uncertainty estimate.
